#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
add_position.py — record a buy in positions.json (the widget's "buy" button
runs this too).

    python3 add_position.py MSFT 10                        # 10 shares, today
    python3 add_position.py SHOP.TO --amount 1000          # 1000 worth, at today's price
    python3 add_position.py MSFT 10 --cost 150 --date 2025-01-02
    python3 add_position.py MSFT 10 --theme "Big tech"
    python3 add_position.py --set-invested 25000           # money you've put in

Any symbol Yahoo Finance lists works (SHOP.TO, VOD.L, 7203.T, BTC-USD...);
ticker_lookup.py search "name" finds one. A new ticker gets its own entry;
an existing one gets another lot (older entry shapes are converted first;
nothing is overwritten). Without --cost the tracker uses that day's closing
price as your cost, marked ≈ in the widget until you fill in the real price.
--amount is in the widget's display currency and needs yfinance to look up
the price. If "_invested" is set, the cost of the buy is added to it. The
widget refreshes a few seconds later.
"""

import argparse
import os
from datetime import datetime

import portfolio_file as pf


def add_lot(raw, ticker, lot, theme=None):
    """Append one purchase (`lot` = {"shares", "date"[, "avgCost"]}) to the
    ticker's entry in the loaded positions file, converting the older entry
    shapes (a bare share count, or {"shares", "avgCost", "purchaseDate"}) to
    the lots shape first; nothing is overwritten. Returns "added" for a new
    ticker, "added a lot to" otherwise. import_positions.py uses this too.
    Raises ValueError for an entry shape it does not know."""
    entry = raw.get(ticker)
    if entry is None:
        raw[ticker] = {"lots": [lot]}
        if theme:
            raw[ticker]["theme"] = theme
        return "added"
    if isinstance(entry, (int, float)) and not isinstance(entry, bool):
        raw[ticker] = {"lots": [{"shares": float(entry)}, lot]}
        return "added a lot to"
    if isinstance(entry, dict) and "lots" in entry:
        entry["lots"].append(lot)
        if theme:
            entry["theme"] = theme
        return "added a lot to"
    if isinstance(entry, dict) and "shares" in entry:
        old_lot = {"shares": float(entry["shares"])}
        if entry.get("purchaseDate"):
            old_lot["date"] = entry["purchaseDate"]
        if entry.get("avgCost") is not None:
            old_lot["avgCost"] = float(entry["avgCost"])
        new_entry = {k: v for k, v in entry.items()
                     if k in ("theme", "currency")}
        new_entry["lots"] = [old_lot, lot]
        if theme:
            new_entry["theme"] = theme
        raw[ticker] = new_entry
        return "added a lot to"
    raise ValueError("unrecognized entry shape for %s" % ticker)


def main():
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("ticker", nargs="?", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("shares", nargs="?", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--amount", default=None,
                    help="buy this much (display currency) instead of a share count")
    ap.add_argument("--cost", default=None,
                    help="price you paid per share (omit: that day's close)")
    ap.add_argument("--date", default=None, help="YYYY-MM-DD (default: today)")
    ap.add_argument("--theme", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--rate", default=None, help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # from the + form's lookup
    ap.add_argument("--set-invested", default=None, metavar="AMOUNT",
                    help="total money you've put in, in the widget's currency; "
                         "used by the 'vs invested' P&L view")
    ap.add_argument("--positions", default=os.path.join(here, "positions.json"))
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.set_invested is not None:
        amount = pf.positive_number(args.set_invested, "--set-invested")
        raw = pf.load(args.positions, create=True)
        raw["_invested"] = amount
        pf.save(args.positions, raw)
        pf.request_refresh(args.positions)
        print("invested set to %s — refreshing" % amount)
        return

    if args.ticker is None or (args.shares is None and args.amount is None):
        pf.fail("need TICKER and SHARES, TICKER --amount MONEY, or --set-invested AMOUNT")
    ticker = pf.ticker_arg(args.ticker)
    cost = pf.positive_number(args.cost, "--cost") if args.cost is not None else None
    today = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    date_str = (args.date or today).strip()
    try:
        if not pf.DATE_RE.match(date_str):
            raise ValueError
        datetime.strptime(date_str, "%Y-%m-%d")
    except ValueError:
        pf.fail("--date must be YYYY-MM-DD")

    rate = pf.positive_number(args.rate, "--rate") if args.rate is not None else None
    if args.amount is not None:
        # money -> shares at the current price (needs yfinance)
        money = pf.positive_number(args.amount, "--amount")
        try:
            import yfinance
            from ticker_lookup import quote
        except ImportError:
            pf.fail("--amount needs yfinance to look up the price; give a share count instead")
        q = quote(ticker, args.positions, yfinance)
        if q.get("error"):
            pf.fail(q["error"])
        if not q.get("displayRate"):
            pf.fail("no exchange rate for %s; give a share count instead" % q.get("currency"))
        per_share = cost if cost is not None else q["price"]
        rate = q["displayRate"]
        shares = round(money / (per_share * rate), 6)
        if cost is None and date_str == today:
            cost = q["price"]        # bought now, at the current price
    else:
        shares = pf.positive_number(args.shares, "shares")

    raw = pf.load(args.positions, create=True)
    lot = {"shares": shares, "date": date_str}
    if cost is not None:
        lot["avgCost"] = cost
    try:
        action = add_lot(raw, ticker, lot, args.theme)
    except ValueError as e:
        pf.fail(str(e))

    # the buy's cost goes into _invested (money put in)
    note = ""
    if raw.get("_invested") is not None:
        per_share = cost if cost is not None else pf.last_price(args.positions, ticker)
        spent = (pf.to_display(args.positions, ticker, per_share, shares, rate)
                 if per_share is not None else None)
        if spent is not None:
            raw["_invested"] = round(float(raw["_invested"]) + spent, 2)
            note = " — invested +%s%.2f (now %s)" % (
                "" if cost is not None else "~", spent, raw["_invested"])
        else:
            note = " — invested unchanged (no price yet; use --set-invested)"

    pf.save(args.positions, raw)
    pf.request_refresh(args.positions)
    basis = "cost %s" % cost if cost is not None else "cost ≈ that day's close"
    print("%s %s: %s sh on %s (%s)%s — refreshing"
          % (action, ticker, shares, date_str, basis, note))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
export.py — the portfolio as four CSV files for Numbers / Excel / a script
(widget_command.sh export runs this for the widget's footer "export" link).

    python3 export.py                      # -> ~/Documents/Portfolio/
    python3 export.py --out ~/Desktop/pf   # somewhere else
    PORTFOLIO_EXPORT_DIR=/some/dir python3 export.py

Output folder: --out, else $PORTFOLIO_EXPORT_DIR, else ~/Documents/Portfolio
(created when missing). Files, each replaced as a whole:

  holdings.csv      one row per purchase (lot) with its cost, then one CASH row
                    per _cash currency
  daily_values.csv  the full day-by-day table (.cache/daily_all.json): value,
                    money in, gain, index close
  sales.csv         the sales recorded in _realized (header only without any)
  dividends.csv     every dividend your shares earned, by ex-date, from the
                    cached payment history: holdings you own now, dated
                    purchases and recorded sales only; amounts at today's
                    exchange rate (header only without any)

UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, comma separated, CRLF line ends, a header row,
ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD), plain numbers ("." decimals, no currency signs or
thousands separators). Prices and costs per share are in the stock's quote
currency (GBp = pence); *_home columns are in the widget's display currency
at today's rate. Text starting with = + - @ gets a leading ' so a
spreadsheet never runs it as a formula.

Reads positions.json and the widget's last refresh (.cache/data.json,
daily_all.json, derived_basis.json, ticker_meta.json); no network, writes nothing into the
widget folder. Prints one line of JSON and nothing else:
{"ok": true, "dir", "dirShown", "path", "files", "rows", "currency"} or
{"error": "..."} (exit 1). Standard library only, so any python3 can run it.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import errno
import json
import math
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime

import portfolio_file as pf
import portfolio_tracker as pt

FILES = ("holdings.csv", "daily_values.csv", "sales.csv", "dividends.csv")
HOLDINGS_HEADER = ["ticker", "name", "theme", "purchase_date", "shares", "cost_per_share",
                   "cost_total", "cost_source", "currency", "price", "value", "fx_rate",
                   "home_currency", "value_home", "cost_home", "gain_home", "gain_pct"]
DAILY_HEADER = ["date", "value", "money_in", "gain", "source", "index_close",
                "index_symbol", "currency"]
SALES_HEADER = ["date", "ticker", "shares", "price", "currency", "proceeds", "cost", "gain",
                "fx_rate", "home_currency", "proceeds_home", "cost_home", "gain_home",
                "purchase_dates"]
DIVIDENDS_HEADER = ["ex_date", "ticker", "per_share", "shares_held", "amount", "currency",
                    "fx_rate", "home_currency", "amount_home"]
# decimals per kind of number
DP_SHARES, DP_COST, DP_PRICE, DP_FX, DP_MONEY, DP_PCT, DP_INDEX = 6, 6, 4, 6, 2, 2, 4
PRIVACY_HINT = ("allow Übersicht to use the Documents folder (System Settings "
                "› Privacy & Security › Files and Folders)")


def reply(obj, code=0):
    print(json.dumps(obj))
    sys.exit(code)


def fnum(x):
    """A finite float, or None (bools, text, NaN and infinities too)."""
    if x is None or isinstance(x, bool):
        return None
    try:
        x = float(x)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return x if math.isfinite(x) else None


def num(x, dp):
    """Plain number text: '.' decimals, no exponent or separators, trailing
    zeros trimmed, -0 -> 0; None / non-finite -> empty cell."""
    x = fnum(x)
    if x is None:
        return ""
    s = "%.*f" % (dp, round(x, dp))
    if "." in s:
        s = s.rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
    return "0" if s in ("-0", "") else s


def text(v):
    """A text cell: whitespace runs -> one space, control characters dropped,
    a leading = + - @ neutralised with ' (spreadsheet formula injection)."""
    if v is None:
        return ""
    s = " ".join(str(v).split())
    s = "".join(ch for ch in s if ord(ch) >= 32 and not 127 <= ord(ch) < 160)
    if s[:1] in ("=", "+", "-", "@"):
        s = "'" + s
    return s


def mul(*xs):
    out = 1.0
    for x in xs:
        x = fnum(x)
        if x is None:
            return None
        out *= x
    return out


def sub(a, b):
    a, b = fnum(a), fnum(b)
    return None if a is None or b is None else a - b


def tilde(path):
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    if home and home != "/" and (path == home or path.startswith(home.rstrip("/") + "/")):
        return "~" + path[len(home.rstrip("/")):]
    return path


def out_dir(arg):
    d = (arg or "").strip() or (os.environ.get("PORTFOLIO_EXPORT_DIR") or "").strip()
    if not d:
        d = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "Documents", "Portfolio")
    return os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(d))


def tcc_protected(folder):
    """True when folder is inside a macOS privacy-protected user folder."""
    home = os.path.realpath(os.path.expanduser("~"))
    f = os.path.realpath(folder)
    for sub in ("Documents", "Desktop", "Downloads"):
        base = os.path.join(home, sub)
        if f == base or f.startswith(base + os.sep):
            return True
    return False


def home_currency(raw, data):
    cur = data.get("currency")
    if isinstance(cur, str) and cur:
        return cur
    return pt.resolve_currency(pt.load_settings(raw)["currency"])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tables

def holdings_rows(path, positions, cash, data, home):
    """One row per lot (tickers a-z, lots in file order), then CASH rows."""
    rows_by_tk = {}
    for p in data.get("positions") or []:
        if isinstance(p, dict) and isinstance(p.get("ticker"), str) and not p.get("watch"):
            rows_by_tk.setdefault(p["ticker"], p)
    out = []
    for tk in sorted(positions):
        entry = positions[tk]
        drow = rows_by_tk.get(tk, {})
        cur = drow.get("currency")
        if not (isinstance(cur, str) and cur):
            cur = entry.get("currency") if isinstance(entry.get("currency"), str) \
                and entry.get("currency").strip() else pt.infer_currency(tk)
        cur = cur.strip()
        theme = drow.get("theme") or entry.get("theme")
        price, rate = fnum(drow.get("price")), fnum(drow.get("fxRate"))
        # data.json's price is rounded for display (2 dp), so shares x price
        # can miss the widget's value by cents: when the refresh saw the same
        # shares, each lot gets its share of the widget's own value instead
        # (the holdings then add up to the widget's total exactly)
        held = sum(lot["shares"] for lot in entry["lots"])
        row_value, row_shares = fnum(drow.get("value")), fnum(drow.get("shares"))
        per_share_home = (row_value / row_shares
                          if row_value is not None and row_shares and price is not None
                          and abs(held - row_shares) <= 1e-9 * max(1.0, abs(held)) else None)
        for lot in entry["lots"]:
            shares = lot["shares"]
            if lot.get("avgCost") is not None:
                cps, source = fnum(lot["avgCost"]), "entered"
            else:
                cps = pf.derived_cost(path, tk, lot.get("date"))
                # the close the tracker used as this lot's cost, else none:
                # the widget counts such a lot at today's price, the CSV
                # doesn't invent a cost
                source = "estimated" if cps is not None else "unknown"
            cost_total = mul(shares, cps)
            value = mul(shares, price)
            value_home = mul(shares, per_share_home) if per_share_home is not None \
                else mul(value, rate)
            cost_home = mul(cost_total, rate)
            gain_home = sub(value_home, cost_home)
            gain_pct = (gain_home / cost_home * 100
                        if gain_home is not None and cost_home else None)
            out.append([text(tk), text(drow.get("name")), text(theme), lot.get("date") or "",
                        num(shares, DP_SHARES), num(cps, DP_COST), num(cost_total, DP_MONEY),
                        source, text(cur), num(price, DP_PRICE), num(value, DP_MONEY),
                        num(rate, DP_FX), text(home), num(value_home, DP_MONEY),
                        num(cost_home, DP_MONEY), num(gain_home, DP_MONEY),
                        num(gain_pct, DP_PCT)])
    rates = data.get("fxRates") if isinstance(data.get("fxRates"), dict) else {}
    for iso in sorted(cash):
        rate = 1.0 if iso == home else fnum(rates.get(iso))
        out.append(["CASH", "cash", "", "", "", "", "", "", text(iso), "",
                    num(cash[iso], DP_MONEY), num(rate, DP_FX), text(home),
                    num(mul(cash[iso], rate), DP_MONEY), "", "", ""])
    return out


def daily_rows(path, data, home):
    """Every row of the full day table, oldest first:
    [date, epoch, value, approx, index level|null, money at work|null]."""
    table = pt.read_json(os.path.join(pf.cache_dir(path), "daily_all.json"), {})
    rows = table.get("rows") if isinstance(table, dict) else None
    rows = [r for r in rows if isinstance(r, list) and len(r) >= 4
            and isinstance(r[0], str) and pf.DATE_RE.match(r[0])] \
        if isinstance(rows, list) else []
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r[0])
    steps = data.get("basisSteps")
    steps = [s for s in steps if isinstance(s, list) and len(s) >= 2
             and fnum(s[0]) is not None and fnum(s[1]) is not None] \
        if isinstance(steps, list) else []
    bench = data.get("benchmark")
    symbol = bench.get("symbol") if isinstance(bench, dict) else None
    symbol = symbol if isinstance(symbol, str) else ""
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        value = fnum(r[2])
        money_in = fnum(r[5]) if len(r) > 5 else None
        if money_in is None and steps and fnum(r[1]) is not None:
            money_in = fnum(pt.basis_at(steps, fnum(r[1])))
        idx = fnum(r[4]) if len(r) > 4 else None
        out.append([r[0], num(value, DP_MONEY), num(money_in, DP_MONEY),
                    num(sub(value, money_in), DP_MONEY),
                    "rebuilt" if r[3] else "recorded", num(idx, DP_INDEX),
                    text(symbol) if idx is not None else "", text(home)])
    return out


def sales_rows(raw, home):
    """_realized, dated sales oldest first (stable), undated ones last."""
    recs = pt.load_realized(raw)
    recs = sorted((r for r in recs if r["date"]), key=lambda r: r["date"]) + \
        [r for r in recs if not r["date"]]
    out = []
    for r in recs:
        dates = sorted({sl["date"] for sl in r["lots"] if sl["date"]})
        out.append([r["date"] or "", text(r["ticker"]), num(r["shares"], DP_SHARES),
                    num(r["price"], DP_PRICE), text(r["currency"]),
                    num(r["proceeds"], DP_MONEY), num(r["basis"], DP_MONEY),
                    num(r["gain"], DP_MONEY), num(r["fxRate"], DP_FX),
                    text(r["displayCurrency"] or home),
                    num(r["proceedsDisplay"], DP_MONEY), num(r["basisDisplay"], DP_MONEY),
                    num(r["gainDisplay"], DP_MONEY), "; ".join(dates)])
    return out


def dividend_rows(path, raw, positions, data, home):
    """Every dividend the shares earned (pt.divs_paid: the payments behind
    the widget's "received" total), by ex-date then ticker; holdings owned
    now only, amounts at today's rate (data.json's fxRate)."""
    meta = pt.read_json(os.path.join(pf.cache_dir(path), "ticker_meta.json"), {})
    if not isinstance(meta, dict):
        meta = {}
    today = datetime.now(pt.MARKET_TZ).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    sold = pt.sold_slices(pt.load_realized(raw))
    rows_by_tk = {}
    for p in data.get("positions") or []:
        if isinstance(p, dict) and isinstance(p.get("ticker"), str) and not p.get("watch"):
            rows_by_tk.setdefault(p["ticker"], p)
    out = []
    for tk in sorted(positions):
        m = meta.get(tk)
        divs = pt.clean_divs(m.get("divs")) if isinstance(m, dict) else None
        if not divs:
            continue
        entry, drow = positions[tk], rows_by_tk.get(tk, {})
        cur = drow.get("currency")
        if not (isinstance(cur, str) and cur):
            cur = entry.get("currency") if isinstance(entry.get("currency"), str) \
                and entry.get("currency").strip() else pt.infer_currency(tk)
        cur = cur.strip()
        fx = fnum(drow.get("fxRate"))
        for d, a, sh in pt.divs_paid(divs, entry["lots"], today, sold.get(tk, ())):
            out.append([d, text(tk), num(a, DP_COST), num(sh, DP_SHARES),
                        num(a * sh, DP_MONEY), text(cur), num(fx, DP_FX), text(home),
                        num(mul(a * sh, fx), DP_MONEY)])
    out.sort(key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1]))
    return out


def write_csv(folder, name, header, rows):
    """<name>.tmp, then an atomic replace: a reader never sees half a file."""
    final = os.path.join(folder, name)
    tmp = final + ".tmp"
    try:
        with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
            w = csv.writer(f)
            w.writerow(header)
            w.writerows(rows)
        os.replace(tmp, final)
    except BaseException:
        try:
            os.remove(tmp)
        except OSError:
            pass
        raise


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- main

class JsonArgs(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    """argparse's usage errors as JSON on stdout, like every other reply."""
    def error(self, message):
        reply({"error": message}, 1)


def main():
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    ap = JsonArgs(description="Write holdings, daily values, sales and dividends as CSV files.")
    ap.add_argument("--positions", default=os.path.join(here, "positions.json"))
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None,
                    help="output folder (default: $PORTFOLIO_EXPORT_DIR, else "
                         "~/Documents/Portfolio)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    path = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(args.positions))
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        reply({"error": "no positions file yet"}, 1)
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            raw = json.load(f)
        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
            raise ValueError("it should contain a JSON object")
        positions, cash, _invested, _settings, _watch = pt.load_positions(path)
    except Exception as e:
        reply({"error": "could not read positions.json: %s" % e}, 1)

    data = pf.load_data(path)
    home = home_currency(raw, data)
    tables = (holdings_rows(path, positions, cash, data, home),
              daily_rows(path, data, home),
              sales_rows(raw, home),
              dividend_rows(path, raw, positions, data, home))

    folder = out_dir(args.out)
    try:
        os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
        for name, header, rows in zip(FILES, (HOLDINGS_HEADER, DAILY_HEADER, SALES_HEADER,
                                              DIVIDENDS_HEADER), tables):
            write_csv(folder, name, header, rows)
    except OSError as e:
        msg = "[Errno %d] %s" % (e.errno, e.strerror) if e.errno and e.strerror else str(e)
        msg = "could not write to %s: %s" % (tilde(folder), msg)
        if e.errno in (errno.EPERM, errno.EACCES):
            msg += " — " + (PRIVACY_HINT if tcc_protected(folder) else "the folder is not writable")
        reply({"error": msg}, 1)

    reply({"ok": True, "dir": folder, "dirShown": tilde(folder),
           "path": os.path.join(folder, FILES[0]), "files": list(FILES),
           "rows": {"holdings": len(tables[0]), "daily": len(tables[1]),
                    "sales": len(tables[2]), "dividends": len(tables[3])},
           "currency": home})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as e:       # never a traceback instead of the JSON line
        reply({"error": "export failed: %s" % e}, 1)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
import_positions.py — add many holdings at once from a pasted list or a CSV
file (the widget's "import a list…" runs this; standard library only).

    python3 import_positions.py --text "KO 10, MSFT 5 at 310 on 2024-03-01"
    python3 import_positions.py --file ~/Downloads/holdings.csv
    python3 import_positions.py --file holdings.csv --commit     # save them

Without --commit nothing is written: the answer is a preview. The output is
one JSON object:

    {"rows": [{"line": 2, "ticker": "MSFT", "shares": 5, "cost": 310,
               "date": "2024-03-01", "ok": true, "note": ""}, ...],
     "ok": 2, "skipped": 1, "format": "lines" | "csv", "columns": {...}}

and with --commit also "added" (lots written), "tickers" (new or extended),
"backup" (the copy of positions.json made first) and "invested" (the money
added to _invested when that figure is kept).

Two formats are understood, told apart automatically:

* one holding per line: a ticker, the number of shares, then optionally the
  price paid per share and the purchase date, in any order —
  "KO 10", "10 KO", "MSFT 5 at 310 on 2024-03-01", "SHOP.TO 12 @ 61.5",
  "VOD.L, 200, 0.98, 12/03/2024". Several holdings may share a line when
  separated by ";" or by a "," before the next holding ("KO 10, MSFT 5",
  "10 KO, 5 MSFT"). A chunk with two stocks in it ("MSFT 5 at 50 KO 1") or
  a price behind a word that is not understood ("KO 10 blah 50") is skipped
  with a note rather than guessed.
* a CSV / TSV export from a broker, with a header row: the ticker column is
  found by its name (symbol, ticker, stock, code, instrument, security…),
  shares by quantity / qty / units / shares / position, the price by cost,
  price, avg cost, average price, book cost, purchase price, unit cost…, a
  total (book value, cost basis, total cost, amount invested) is divided by
  the shares, and the date by date / purchase date / trade date / acquired.
  An "Average Cost" style column beats a bare "Price" one; a bare "Price"
  next to a "Market Price" is used with a "check it" note. The separator is
  the one most lines share (";" before "\t", "|" and "," on a tie), trying
  the next one when no header is found. Without a header the columns are
  ticker, shares, price, date in that order, and the free-form reading wins
  when it finds more holdings ("ITW 1, MSFT 2" is not a CSV).

A line that is not a holding (a sale with negative shares, a heading, a
total row, a name without a ticker) is skipped with a note — nothing stops
the rest. Numbers may carry currency signs and thousands separators
("$1,234.50", "1.234,50"); dates may be YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD, DD.MM.YYYY,
DD/MM/YYYY, DD-MM-YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY (the first number is the day unless it
cannot be), or "Mar 1 2024" / "1 March 2024" / "Mar 1, 2024". Exchange
prefixes become Yahoo suffixes: "TSX:SHOP" -> SHOP.TO, "LSE:VOD" -> VOD.L
(with a note), "NYSE:KO" / "KO:NYSE" -> KO. Files may be UTF-8, UTF-16 or
Windows (cp1252) text.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import io
import json
import math
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
from datetime import date, datetime

import portfolio_file as pf
from add_position import add_lot

MAX_ROWS = 500                  # holdings one import may add
MAX_TEXT = 2 * 1024 * 1024      # bytes read from a file
BACKUP_KEEP = 5                 # import backups kept (the newest)

TICKER_WORDS = ("symbol", "ticker", "stock", "code", "instrument", "security", "asset", "isin/ticker",
                "ticker symbol", "symbol/cusip", "product")
SHARE_WORDS = ("shares", "quantity", "qty", "units", "position", "holding", "number of shares", "share count",
               "amount of shares", "no. of shares", "qty.", "volume", "count")
COST_WORDS = ("avg cost", "average cost", "avg. cost", "avg price", "average price", "avg. price", "cost/share",
              "cost per share", "price paid", "purchase price", "buy price", "unit cost", "unit price",
              "cost basis per share", "average cost basis", "entry price", "price", "cost", "open price",
              "acquisition price", "avg", "book cost/share")
TOTAL_WORDS = ("book value", "book cost", "cost basis", "total cost", "amount invested", "invested", "total",
               "cost basis total", "purchase value", "total paid", "amount")
DATE_WORDS = ("purchase date", "trade date", "date acquired", "acquired", "open date", "date", "bought",
              "buy date", "settlement date", "acquisition date", "first purchase")
SKIP_TOTAL_RE = re.compile(r"^(total|totals|grand total|sum|cash|balance)\b", re.I)
NUM_RE = re.compile(r"^[-+]?(\d+([.,]\d+)*|[.,]\d+)$")
DATE_ISO = re.compile(r"^(\d{4})-(\d{1,2})-(\d{1,2})$")
DATE_DOT = re.compile(r"^(\d{1,2})[./](\d{1,2})[./](\d{4})$")
DATE_DASH = re.compile(r"^(\d{1,2})-(\d{1,2})-(\d{4})$")
DATE_YSLASH = re.compile(r"^(\d{4})/(\d{1,2})/(\d{1,2})$")
DAY_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{1,2})(?:st|nd|rd|th)?$", re.I)
YEAR_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}$")
MONTHS = ("january", "february", "march", "april", "may", "june", "july", "august", "september", "october",
          "november", "december")
EXCHANGE_SUFFIX = {"TSX": ".TO", "TSE": ".TO", "TSXV": ".V", "CVE": ".V", "CSE": ".CN", "NEO": ".NE", "LSE": ".L",
                   "LON": ".L", "XETRA": ".DE", "ETR": ".DE", "FRA": ".F", "ASX": ".AX", "HKEX": ".HK", "HKG": ".HK",
                   "NYSE": "", "NASDAQ": "", "AMEX": "", "ARCA": "", "BATS": ""}
# a currency code after the ticker ("KO 10 at 50 USD") is not a second stock
CURRENCY_WORDS = ("usd", "eur", "gbp", "gbx", "cad", "chf", "sek", "nok", "dkk", "jpy", "aud", "nzd", "hkd")
# a "," splits a line before the next holding: "KO 10, MSFT 5" / "10 KO, 5 MSFT"
# — but not before "on 2024-03-01", "at 50", "10 shares" (the same holding)
_FILLER = r"(?:at|for|on|cost|price|date|bought|x|shares|sh|units|of)\b"
_TICK = r"[A-Za-z^][A-Za-z0-9.:\-=&]*"
# number first ("10 KO, 5 MSFT"): only an upper-case ticker that is not a
# currency ("KO 10, 50 USD" / "KO 10, 50 each" are one holding with a price)
_UTICK = r"(?!(?:%s)(?![A-Za-z0-9]))[A-Z^][A-Z0-9.:\-=&]*(?![a-z])" % "|".join(w.upper() for w in CURRENCY_WORDS)
_CNUM = r"\d{1,20}(?:[.,]\d{1,20}){0,8}"     # bounded: no blow-up on long "1,1,1,…" runs
# never at a comma inside a number: "1,000, MSFT 5" splits after "1,000" only
# (a comma right after a digit needs a space after it)
COMMA_SPLIT = re.compile(r"(?:(?<!\d),\s*|(?<=\d),\s+)(?!(?i:%s))(?=(?:%s\s+(?!(?i:%s))%s|%s\s+\d))"
                         % (_FILLER, _CNUM, _FILLER, _UTICK, _TICK))
COMMA_SPLIT_MAX = 2000          # a longer line is one chunk (no comma split)
COST_TIER2 = ("avg", "average", "book", "purchase", "paid", "unit", "cost", "share", "entry", "acquisition", "buy")
MARKET_PREFIX = ("market", "last", "current", "close", "mkt")
PRICE_PREFIX = ("@", "at", "for", "cost", "price")
DATE_PREFIX = ("on", "date", "bought")
CURRENCY_SIGNS = re.compile(r"^(?:[A-Z]{1,3}\$|US\$|CA\$|[$€£¥₹]|[A-Z]{3})?\s*(.*?)\s*(?:[$€£¥₹]|[A-Z]{3})?$")


def reply(obj, code=0):
    json.dump(obj, sys.stdout, allow_nan=False)
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
    sys.exit(code)


def clean_number(text):
    """"$1,234.50" / "1.234,50" / "12,5" / "(300)" -> float or None."""
    s = str(text or "").strip()
    if not s:
        return None
    neg = s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")")
    s = s.strip("()").strip()
    m = CURRENCY_SIGNS.match(s)
    if m:
        s = m.group(1).strip()
    s = s.replace(" ", "").replace(" ", "").replace("'", "")
    if s.startswith(("+", "-", "−")):
        neg = neg or s[0] in "-−"
        s = s[1:]
    if not NUM_RE.match(s):
        return None
    if "," in s and "." in s:
        # the last separator is the decimal one: 1,234.50 or 1.234,50
        if s.rfind(",") > s.rfind("."):
            s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
        else:
            s = s.replace(",", "")
    elif "," in s:
        parts = s.split(",")
        # 1,234 or 12,345,678 = thousands; 12,5 = a decimal comma
        if len(parts) > 2 or (len(parts) == 2 and len(parts[1]) == 3 and len(parts[0]) <= 3):
            s = s.replace(",", "")
        else:
            s = s.replace(",", ".")
    elif s.count(".") > 1:
        # 1.234.567 = thousands with dots
        s = s.replace(".", "")
    try:
        v = float(s)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if not math.isfinite(v):
        return None
    return -v if neg else v


def clean_date(text):
    """A purchase date as YYYY-MM-DD, or None. Not after today."""
    s = str(text or "").strip()
    if not s:
        return None
    parts = month_date(s)
    if parts is None:
        s = s.split("T")[0].split(" ")[0]
        m = DATE_ISO.match(s) or DATE_YSLASH.match(s)
        if m:
            y, a, b = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
            parts = [(y, a, b)]
        else:
            m = DATE_DOT.match(s) or DATE_DASH.match(s)
            if not m:
                return None
            a, b, y = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
            parts = [(y, b, a), (y, a, b)]        # day first, else month first
    for y, mo, d in parts:
        try:
            dt = date(y, mo, d)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if dt > date.today() or y < 1900:
            return None
        return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    return None


def month_of(word):
    """"Mar" / "March" / "Sept" / "mar." -> 3, else None."""
    w = str(word or "").strip().strip(".,").lower()
    if len(w) < 3 or not w.isalpha():
        return None
    if w == "sept":
        return 9
    for i, name in enumerate(MONTHS):
        if name.startswith(w):
            return i + 1
    return None


def month_date(s):
    """"Mar 1 2024" / "1 Mar 2024" / "Mar 1, 2024" -> [(y, m, d)], else None."""
    words = s.replace(",", " ").replace(".", " ").split()
    if len(words) != 3 or not YEAR_RE.match(words[2]):
        return None
    for mw, dw in ((words[0], words[1]), (words[1], words[0])):
        mo, dm = month_of(mw), DAY_RE.match(dw)
        if mo and dm:
            return [(int(words[2]), mo, int(dm.group(1)))]
    return None


def looks_like_date(text):
    """True for text written like a date (2031-01-01, 01.03.2024, Mar 1 2024),
    whether or not it is a real, past day (clean_date says that)."""
    s = str(text or "").strip()
    if not s:
        return False
    if month_date(s) is not None:
        return True
    s = s.split("T")[0].split(" ")[0]
    return any(r.match(s) for r in (DATE_ISO, DATE_YSLASH, DATE_DOT, DATE_DASH))


def split_ticker(text):
    """-> (symbol or None, note). A Yahoo-style symbol, upper-cased.
    "KO:NYSE", "NYSE:KO" and "KO.US" (some brokers) become KO; an exchange
    with a Yahoo suffix adds it: "TSX:SHOP" / "SHOP:TSX" -> SHOP.TO, with
    the note "TSX:SHOP read as SHOP.TO"."""
    s = str(text or "").strip().upper().strip("'\"")
    if not s:
        return None, ""
    given, suffix = s, ""
    if ":" in s:
        a, b = [x.strip() for x in s.split(":", 1)]
        if a in EXCHANGE_SUFFIX:
            s, suffix = b, EXCHANGE_SUFFIX[a]
        elif b in EXCHANGE_SUFFIX:
            s, suffix = a, EXCHANGE_SUFFIX[b]
        else:
            s = b if len(a) > len(b) else a
    if s.endswith(".US") and len(s) > 3:
        s = s[:-3]
    s = s.strip()
    if NUM_RE.match(s) or not pf.TICKER_RE.match(s) or looks_like_date(s):
        return None, ""
    if suffix and not s.endswith(suffix):
        s += suffix
        return s, "%s read as %s" % (given, s)
    return s, ""


def clean_ticker(text):
    """A Yahoo-style symbol, upper-cased, or None (see split_ticker)."""
    return split_ticker(text)[0]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- free lines
def join_month_dates(toks):
    """["MSFT", "5", "Mar", "1", "2024"] -> ["MSFT", "5", "Mar 1 2024"]: a
    month word with its day and 4-digit year becomes one date token
    ("Mar 1 2024" or "1 Mar 2024"). Only a real, past day is joined, and an
    upper-case month word before any ticker stays a ticker ("DEC 12 1500" is
    12 shares of DEC at 1500)."""
    out = list(toks)
    i = 0
    seen_ticker = False
    while i < len(out):
        w = out[i]
        if month_of(w) and not (w.strip(".,") == w.strip(".,").upper() and not seen_ticker):
            nxt = out[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(out) else ""
            nxt2 = out[i + 2] if i + 2 < len(out) else ""
            prev = out[i - 1] if i > 0 else ""
            if DAY_RE.match(nxt) and YEAR_RE.match(nxt2) and clean_date(" ".join(out[i:i + 3])):
                out[i:i + 3] = [" ".join(out[i:i + 3])]
            elif i > 0 and DAY_RE.match(prev) and YEAR_RE.match(nxt) and clean_date(" ".join(out[i - 1:i + 2])):
                out[i - 1:i + 2] = [" ".join(out[i - 1:i + 2])]
                i -= 1
        elif not seen_ticker and clean_number(w) is None and split_ticker(w)[0]:
            seen_ticker = True
        i += 1
    return out


def parse_free_line(line):
    """One or more holdings from a free-form line -> list of row dicts
    (ok / note filled in)."""
    out = []
    text = line.strip()
    if not text:
        return out
    # "KO 10, MSFT 5" / "10 KO, 5 MSFT" / "KO 10; MSFT 5": split where a
    # separator is followed by the next holding
    chunks = []
    for part in re.split(r"\s*;\s*", text):
        chunks.extend(COMMA_SPLIT.split(part) if len(part) <= COMMA_SPLIT_MAX else [part])
    for chunk in chunks:
        # whitespace splits; a comma does too, unless it sits inside a number
        # ("$61,234.50", "1,000") — "KO,10" is split as well
        toks = []
        for t in chunk.strip().split():
            t = t.strip(",")
            if not t:
                continue
            if "," in t and clean_number(t) is None and clean_date(t) is None:
                toks.extend(x for x in t.split(",") if x)
            else:
                toks.append(t)
        toks = join_month_dates(toks)
        if not toks:
            continue
        ticker, shares, cost, dt = None, None, None, None
        expect = None
        notes = []
        unclear = two = bad_date = False
        after_unknown = False       # the previous token was a word that got "'x' ignored"
        for k, raw in enumerate(toks):
            was_unknown, after_unknown = after_unknown, False
            low = raw.lower().strip(":")
            if low in PRICE_PREFIX:
                expect = "cost"
                continue
            if low in DATE_PREFIX:
                expect = "date"
                continue
            if low in ("x", "×", "shares", "sh", "units", "of"):
                continue
            if ticker is not None and low in CURRENCY_WORDS:
                continue
            d = clean_date(raw)
            if d is None and looks_like_date(raw):
                bad_date = True                 # "on 2031-01-01": a typo, not today
                expect = None
                continue
            if d and (expect in (None, "date")):
                dt = d
                expect = None
                continue
            n = clean_number(raw.lstrip("@"))
            if n is not None:
                if expect == "cost" or (shares is not None and cost is None):
                    cost = n
                    if was_unknown and expect != "cost":
                        unclear = True          # "KO 10 blah 50": is 50 the price?
                elif shares is None:
                    shares = n
                else:
                    notes.append("extra number %s ignored" % raw)
                expect = None
                continue
            tk, tk_note = split_ticker(raw)
            nxt = toks[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(toks) else ""
            if tk and ticker is None:
                ticker = tk
                if tk_note:
                    notes.append(tk_note)
            elif tk and (shares is not None or cost is not None) and raw == raw.upper() \
                    and clean_number(nxt.lstrip("@")) is not None:
                two = True                      # "MSFT 5 at 50 KO 1"
            elif ticker is not None:
                notes.append("'%s' ignored" % raw)
                after_unknown = True
            expect = None
        fail = None
        if bad_date:
            fail = "date in the future or not a real date — check it"
        elif two:
            fail = "two stocks on one line — put each on its own line"
        elif unclear:
            fail = "price unclear — write it as %s 10 at 50" % (ticker or "KO")
        out.append(make_row(ticker, shares, cost, dt, notes, chunk.strip(), fail=fail))
    return out


def make_row(ticker, shares, cost, dt, notes, text, fail=None):
    """A row dict; fail (a note) marks a row that looks like a holding but
    is not imported because a part of it is a guess."""
    row = {"ticker": ticker, "shares": shares, "cost": cost, "date": dt, "ok": False, "note": "", "text": text[:80]}
    if ticker is None:
        row["note"] = "no ticker found"
    elif isinstance(fail, str) and fail:
        row["note"] = fail
    elif shares is None:
        row["note"] = "no share count"
    elif shares < 0:
        row["note"] = "a sale (negative shares) — not imported"
    elif shares == 0:
        row["note"] = "0 shares"
    elif cost is not None and cost <= 0:
        row["note"] = "price must be above 0"
    else:
        row["ok"] = True
        row["shares"] = round(float(shares), 6)
        if cost is not None:
            row["cost"] = round(float(cost), 6)
    if notes and row["ok"]:
        row["note"] = "; ".join(notes)[:120]
    return row


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- csv
def sniff(text):
    """-> [(delimiter, rows), ...] for CSV-looking text, the likeliest first
    (most fields per line; ";" before tab, "|" and "," on a tie, so
    "KO;1,000" splits on ";"), or [] when nothing looks like a CSV."""
    lines = [ln for ln in text.splitlines()[:40] if ln.strip()]
    found = []
    for order, d in enumerate((";", "\t", "|", ",")):
        counts = [ln.count(d) for ln in lines]
        with_d = [c for c in counts if c >= 1]
        # most lines carry the delimiter (a heading like "Account: 1234" or a
        # blank line above the header is fine) and at least two of them do
        if len(with_d) >= 2 and len(with_d) >= 0.6 * len(lines):
            found.append((-sum(with_d) / len(with_d), order, d))
    found.sort()
    out = []
    for _, _, d in found:
        try:   # a delimiter the csv module trips over (an unclosed quote) is dropped
            out.append((d, list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text), delimiter=d))))
        except csv.Error:
            continue
    return out


def header_roles(c):
    """-> {role: score} for one lower-cased header cell (higher = better;
    a cost "tier 2" names what was paid, tier 1 is a bare price / cost)."""
    roles = {}
    if c in TICKER_WORDS or c.endswith((" symbol", " ticker")):
        roles["ticker"] = 2 if c in TICKER_WORDS else 1
    if c in SHARE_WORDS or c.startswith(("quantity", "qty", "shares", "units")):
        roles["shares"] = 2 if c in SHARE_WORDS else 1
    if c in DATE_WORDS or c.endswith(" date") or c.startswith("date "):
        roles["date"] = 2 if c in DATE_WORDS else 1
    if (c in COST_WORDS or any(c.startswith(w + " ") for w in ("avg", "average"))
            or c.endswith(("/share", " per share", " price", " cost"))) \
            and not c.startswith(MARKET_PREFIX) and c not in TOTAL_WORDS:
        roles["cost"] = 1 if c in ("price", "cost") or not any(w in c for w in COST_TIER2) else 2
    if (c in TOTAL_WORDS or c.endswith((" value", " basis"))) and not c.startswith(("market", "current", "mkt")):
        roles["total"] = 2 if c in TOTAL_WORDS else 1
    return roles


def find_header(rows):
    """(index, column map, price_guess) of the header row (within the first
    10 rows), or (None, {}, False) when no cell names a ticker column. Each
    cell serves one role; per role the best-named cell wins, the leftmost
    on a tie. price_guess: the price is a bare "Price" column while the file
    also has a market / last / current price column."""
    for i, row in enumerate(rows[:10]):
        cells = [c.strip().lower().strip('"') for c in row]
        roles = [header_roles(c) if c else {} for c in cells]
        cols, used = {}, set()
        for role in ("ticker", "shares", "date", "cost", "total"):
            best = None
            for j, r in enumerate(roles):
                if j in used or role not in r:
                    continue
                if best is None or r[role] > roles[best][role]:
                    best = j
            if best is not None:
                cols[role] = best
                used.add(best)
        if "ticker" in cols:
            price_guess = "cost" in cols and roles[cols["cost"]]["cost"] == 1 and \
                any(c.startswith(MARKET_PREFIX) for j, c in enumerate(cells) if j != cols["cost"])
            return i, cols, price_guess
    return None, {}, False


def parse_csv_rows(rows, delim, header=None):
    """-> (row dicts, column map). header: find_header(rows) when known."""
    header_i, cols, price_guess = header if header is not None else find_header(rows)
    out = []
    if header_i is None:
        cols = {"ticker": 0, "shares": 1, "cost": 2, "date": 3}
        body = rows
        first_line = 1
    else:
        body = rows[header_i + 1:]
        first_line = header_i + 2
    for k, row in enumerate(body):
        line_no = first_line + k
        cells = [c.strip() for c in row]
        if not any(cells):
            continue
        text = delim.join(cells)

        def cell(key):
            j = cols.get(key)
            return cells[j] if j is not None and j < len(cells) else ""
        if SKIP_TOTAL_RE.match(cell("ticker") or (cells[0] if cells else "")):
            out.append(dict(make_row(None, None, None, None, [], text), note="a total row — skipped", line=line_no))
            continue
        ticker, tk_note = split_ticker(cell("ticker"))
        shares = clean_number(cell("shares"))
        cost = clean_number(cell("cost")) if cols.get("cost") is not None else None
        notes = [tk_note] if tk_note else []
        if cost is None and cols.get("total") is not None and shares:
            total = clean_number(cell("total"))
            if total is not None and total > 0:
                cost = total / shares
                notes.append("price = %s ÷ shares" % cell("total"))
        elif cost is not None and price_guess:
            notes.append('used the "Price" column as what you paid — check it')
        dt = clean_date(cell("date")) if cols.get("date") is not None else None
        fail = None
        if cols.get("date") is not None and cell("date") and dt is None:
            if looks_like_date(cell("date")):
                fail = "date in the future or not a real date — check it"
            else:
                notes.append("date '%s' not understood" % cell("date")[:20])
        r = make_row(ticker, shares, cost, dt, notes, text, fail=fail)
        r["line"] = line_no
        out.append(r)
    return out, cols


def parse_lines(text):
    out = []
    for i, line in enumerate(text.split("\n"), 1):
        if not line.strip() or line.strip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        for r in parse_free_line(line):
            r["line"] = i
            out.append(r)
    return out


def parse_text(text):
    """-> (rows, format, columns). A CSV with a header row is read as a CSV;
    without one, the free-form reading wins unless the CSV reading finds at
    least as many holdings ("ITW 1, MSFT 2" and "KO 1,000" are lines)."""
    text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
    if text.startswith("\ufeff"):
        text = text[1:]
    cands = sniff(text)
    pick = None
    for delim, rows in cands:
        header = find_header(rows)
        if header[0] is not None:
            pick = (delim, rows, header)
            break
    if pick is None and cands:
        pick = (cands[0][0], cands[0][1], (None, {}, False))
    if pick is None:
        return parse_lines(text), "lines", {}
    delim, rows, header = pick
    parsed, cols = parse_csv_rows(rows, delim, header)
    csv_ok = sum(1 for r in parsed if r["ok"])
    lines = parse_lines(text)
    lines_ok = sum(1 for r in lines if r["ok"])
    if header[0] is not None:
        keep_csv = csv_ok > 0 or lines_ok == 0
    else:
        keep_csv = csv_ok > 0 and csv_ok >= lines_ok
    if keep_csv:
        return parsed, "csv", dict(cols)
    return lines, "lines", {}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- commit
def backup_positions(path):
    """A dated copy next to the file (positions.backup-<stamp>-import.json),
    keeping the newest BACKUP_KEEP import backups. None when nothing to copy."""
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None
    folder = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    stamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    name = "positions.backup-%s-import.json" % stamp
    shutil.copy2(path, os.path.join(folder, name))
    olds = sorted(f for f in os.listdir(folder)
                  if re.match(r"^positions\.backup-\d{8}-\d{6}-import\.json$", f))
    for f in olds[:-BACKUP_KEEP]:
        try:
            os.remove(os.path.join(folder, f))
        except OSError:
            pass
    return name


def commit(path, rows):
    raw = pf.load(path, create=True)
    backup = backup_positions(path)
    added, tickers, spent, unknown = 0, [], 0.0, 0
    today = date.today().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    for r in rows:
        if not r["ok"]:
            continue
        lot = {"shares": r["shares"], "date": r["date"] or today}
        if r["cost"] is not None:
            lot["avgCost"] = r["cost"]
        try:
            add_lot(raw, r["ticker"], lot)
        except ValueError as e:
            r["ok"] = False
            r["note"] = str(e)
            continue
        added += 1
        if r["ticker"] not in tickers:
            tickers.append(r["ticker"])
        if raw.get("_invested") is not None:
            per_share = r["cost"] if r["cost"] is not None else pf.last_price(path, r["ticker"])
            value = pf.to_display(path, r["ticker"], per_share, r["shares"]) if per_share else None
            if value is None:
                unknown += 1
            else:
                spent += value
    invested = None
    if raw.get("_invested") is not None and added:
        raw["_invested"] = round(float(raw["_invested"]) + spent, 2)
        invested = {"added": round(spent, 2), "now": raw["_invested"], "unknown": unknown}
    pf.save(path, raw)
    pf.request_refresh(path)
    return {"added": added, "tickers": tickers, "backup": backup, "invested": invested}


def main():
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--text", default=None, help="the pasted list")
    ap.add_argument("--file", default=None, help="a CSV / TSV / text file")
    ap.add_argument("--commit", action="store_true", help="write the holdings (default: preview only)")
    ap.add_argument("--positions", default=os.path.join(here, "positions.json"))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.text is None and args.file is None:
        reply({"error": "give --text or --file"}, 1)
    text = args.text or ""
    if args.file is not None:
        path = os.path.expanduser(args.file.strip())
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                data = f.read(MAX_TEXT + 1)
        except OSError as e:
            reply({"error": "cannot read the file: %s" % (e.strerror or e)}, 1)
        if len(data) > MAX_TEXT:
            reply({"error": "the file is larger than 2 MB"}, 1)
        # UTF-16 only with a byte-order mark or many NUL bytes: an even-length
        # Windows (cp1252) file also "decodes" as UTF-16, into nonsense
        if data[:2] in (b"\xff\xfe", b"\xfe\xff") or data.count(b"\x00") >= max(1, len(data) // 5):
            encodings = ("utf-16", "utf-8-sig", "cp1252", "latin-1")
        else:
            encodings = ("utf-8-sig", "cp1252", "latin-1")
        for enc in encodings:
            try:
                text = data.decode(enc)
                if "\x00" not in text:
                    break
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, LookupError):
                continue
        else:
            reply({"error": "the file is not text"}, 1)
    if len(text) > MAX_TEXT:
        reply({"error": "the list is too long (2 MB at most)"}, 1)
    try:
        rows, fmt, cols = parse_text(text)
    except csv.Error:
        reply({"error": "the file has a line the widget cannot read (an unclosed quote?)"}, 1)
    if len(rows) > MAX_ROWS:
        for r in rows[MAX_ROWS:]:
            r["ok"] = False
            r["note"] = "over %d rows — not imported" % MAX_ROWS
    ok = [r for r in rows if r["ok"]]
    out = {"rows": rows, "ok": len(ok), "skipped": len(rows) - len(ok), "format": fmt, "columns": cols}
    if not rows:
        out["error"] = "nothing to import — one holding per line: ticker and shares (KO 10)"
        reply(out, 0)
    if args.commit:
        if not ok:
            out["error"] = "no holding to add"
            reply(out, 0)
        buf = io.StringIO()
        try:
            import contextlib
            with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
                res = commit(args.positions, ok)
        except SystemExit:
            msg = buf.getvalue().strip()
            out["error"] = msg[len("error: "):] if msg.startswith("error: ") else msg or "could not save"
            reply(out, 1)
        except Exception as e:
            out["error"] = "could not save: %s" % e
            reply(out, 1)
        out.update(res)
    reply(out, 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
portfolio_tracker.py
--------------------
Reads positions.json, fetches quotes from Yahoo Finance (yfinance) in
parallel, and prints ONE JSON blob for the widget. widget_command.sh runs it
in the background; you can also run it by hand to debug:

    python3 portfolio_tracker.py --json --positions positions.json

What it computes:
  * value, day change (split into price vs exchange-rate effect), cost basis, P&L
    and weight per position; totals; movers ranked by dollar impact;
    top-5 concentration; themes (your "theme" tags, else Yahoo's sector)
  * a value history: every run appends a snapshot {t, v} to
    .cache/history.jsonl. Graphs use those real values and fill any stretch
    without snapshots (before the first one, or while the Mac slept) by
    reconstructing current shares x historical closes, flagged "approx"
    (≈ in the widget's hover). 1D = the latest trading session.
  * history is DATE-AWARE: a reconstructed day counts only the lots bought on
    or before it, so "what was my portfolio worth on March 3rd" is answered
    with what you held then. "daily" is the day-by-day table (recorded
    end-of-day value, else that day's closes), "basisSteps" the money at work
    over time (so P&L and range changes don't mistake a deposit for a gain),
    and "sectors" each sector's % performance per range (current holdings).
  * volatility: per stock, the annualised standard deviation of daily
    returns over the last 3 months, plus a 1-10 score (see volatility()).
    The portfolio's own volatility comes from its reconstructed daily value,
    so diversification is counted.
  * a benchmark index ("_settings.benchmark", default per home currency,
    see DEFAULT_BENCHMARKS): its level in the display currency at every
    graph point and every day, for the comparison line. Comparison only —
    never part of a total, a snapshot or the missing/stale lists.
  * a backtest ("backtest"): before the first purchase, what TODAY's holdings
    would have done ("as held now" / "as weighted now", see
    backtest_series()). Its own series — never in the history, the day
    table, the snapshots or level_adjust(); one scale factor per mode makes
    it meet the real graph at its first day.
  * upcoming earnings (+ options-implied move when within 30 days), yearly
    dividend estimate, 50-day sparklines, optional macOS alerts.

Settings live in positions.json under "_settings" (see the README).

Resilience: daily/hourly bars are cached for BARS_TTL while the ticker's
market is open (or in US pre/after hours) and, once it has closed, until
it opens again (BARS_MAX_AGE at most), so a normal refresh is one request
per ticker. A ticker that fails falls back to its last price
(marked stale); one that never had a price (typo, delisted) is skipped and
reported in "missingTickers" rather than failing the whole run.

Long price history (two tiers): a normal refresh only ever downloads one
year of daily closes. Anything older lives in .cache/history_bars.json,
filled by a separate background run (widget_command.sh starts it when the
refresh leaves .cache/history.needed behind):

    python3 portfolio_tracker.py --fetch-history --positions positions.json

It reaches back to the earliest purchase date or "_settings.backtestYears"
(3, 5, 10 or "max"; default 5), whichever is earlier, and later runs only
add the new days. The full day-by-day table goes to .cache/daily_all.json;
data.json carries the newest DAILY_SEND days and older ones are read with

    python3 portfolio_tracker.py --positions positions.json --days-before 2024-01-02 --days-count 400

Exit codes: 0 = success (stdout is valid JSON); 3 = stdout is valid JSON, but
every holding's price request failed (last known prices, marked stale):
commit it and back off; anything else = do not commit cache.

def downsample(points, start, end, n=POINTS_PER_SERIES):
    """At most n points spread evenly over TIME [start, end]: the first point
    plus the last point of each of n-1 equal time buckets. (Picking by index
    let a dense run of recent snapshots eat most of the point budget.)"""
    if len(points) <= n:
        return points
    span = max(1, end - start)
    buckets = {}
    for p in points:
        buckets[min(n - 2, max(0, int((p[0] - start) * (n - 1) / span)))] = p
    picked = [buckets[b] for b in sorted(buckets)]
    return ([points[0]] if picked[0] is not points[0] else []) + picked


def volatility(closes, days=VOL_DAYS):

    Volatility = standard deviation of the last `days` daily log returns,
    x sqrt(252). Score = one point per 10 percentage points, clamped to 1-10:
    utilities land around 2, a typical large cap 3-4, chip makers 6-8,
    speculative small caps 10. Fixed bands rather than a rank, so a score
    means the same in every portfolio and doesn't shift when you add a
    stock. (None, None) with fewer than VOL_MIN_RETURNS returns (new IPOs).
    Yahoo's closes are split-adjusted, so splits don't show up as moves."""
    c = [x for x in closes[-(days + 1):] if x and x > 0]
    vol = annualised_vol([math.log(b / a) for a, b in zip(c, c[1:])])
    return vol, vol_score(vol)


def annualised_vol(log_returns):
    if len(log_returns) < VOL_MIN_RETURNS:
        return None
    mean = sum(log_returns) / len(log_returns)
    var = sum((r - mean) ** 2 for r in log_returns) / (len(log_returns) - 1)
    return math.sqrt(var) * math.sqrt(252) * 100

    """NaN/inf -> None, recursively. Python's json writes bare NaN, which the
    wrapper's Python check accepts but the widget's JSON.parse rejects."""
    if isinstance(x, float):
        return x if math.isfinite(x) else None
    if isinstance(x, dict):
        return {k: json_safe(v) for k, v in x.items()}
    if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)):
        return [json_safe(v) for v in x]
    return x


def rnd(x, p=2):
    if x is None:
        return None
    try:
        if isinstance(x, float) and (math.isnan(x) or math.isinf(x)):
            return None
    except TypeError:
        return None
    return round(float(x), p)

# exchange clocks (13.5): (time zone, local open, local close), Monday to
# Friday; lunch breaks and holidays are ignored. No suffix (and ^indexes)
# = the US clock of market_session. They slow the refresh down while every
# market held is closed and keep the daily / hourly bars from being
# downloaded again at night (symbol_session, refresh_after_for).
EXCHANGE_HOURS = {
    ".TO": ("America/Toronto", "09:30", "16:00"), ".V": ("America/Toronto", "09:30", "16:00"),

    ".TA": ("Asia/Jerusalem", "10:00", "17:25"),
}
# crypto ("BTC-USD": a currency after the dash) trades around the clock,
# and so do exchange rates ("EURUSD=X") as far as the refresh is concerned
CRYPTO_QUOTES = ("USD", "EUR", "GBP", "CAD", "JPY", "AUD", "CHF", "NZD", "SEK", "NOK",
                 "DKK", "HKD", "SGD", "KRW", "INR", "BRL", "MXN", "ZAR", "CNY", "PLN",
                 "TRY", "BTC", "ETH", "USDT", "USDC")   # a crypto pair's quote side
# BTC-USD, ETH-BTC: crypto (open around the clock); KO-PRA (a preferred): not
CRYPTO_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Z0-9]+-(?:%s)$" % "|".join(CRYPTO_QUOTES))


def local_epoch(day, hm, tz):
    """epoch of `day` (a date) at "HH:MM" on the clock of `tz`"""
    h, m = hm.split(":")
    return int(datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, int(h), int(m), tzinfo=tz).timestamp())


def symbol_session(symbol, now=None):
    """(state, last_close_epoch, next_open_epoch) of a symbol's exchange at
    `now` (epoch; None = now_epoch()). state: open | pre | after | closed —
    pre/after only on the US clock (no suffix, ^indexes: 04:00-09:30 and
    16:00-20:00 ET); other exchanges are open or closed (EXCHANGE_HOURS).
    Crypto and exchange rates are always open. last_close: the latest
    weekday close at or before now; next_open: the next start of a session
    (US: of pre-market or the open) after now."""
    now = int(now if now is not None else now_epoch())
    sym = str(symbol or "").strip().upper()
    if sym.endswith("=X") or CRYPTO_RE.match(sym):
        return "open", now, now
    hours = None
    if not sym.startswith("^"):
        for suffix, h in EXCHANGE_HOURS.items():
            if sym.endswith(suffix):
                hours = h
                break
    tz = None
    if hours:
        try:
            tz = ZoneInfo(hours[0])
        except Exception:
            hours = None
    if not hours:
        tz = MARKET_TZ
        local = datetime.fromtimestamp(now, tz)
        state = market_session(local)
        starts, close_hm = ("04:00", "09:30"), "16:00"
    else:
        local = datetime.fromtimestamp(now, tz)
        minutes = local.hour * 60 + local.minute
        o, c = [int(x[:2]) * 60 + int(x[3:]) for x in hours[1:]]
        state = "open" if local.weekday() < 5 and o <= minutes < c else "closed"
        starts, close_hm = (hours[1],), hours[2]
    day, last_close = local.date(), None
    for _ in range(10):
        if day.weekday() < 5:
            t = local_epoch(day, close_hm, tz)
            if t <= now:
                last_close = t
                break
        day -= timedelta(days=1)
    day, next_open = local.date(), None
    for _ in range(10):
        if day.weekday() < 5:
            for hm in starts:
                t = local_epoch(day, hm, tz)
                if t > now:
                    next_open = t
                    break
            if next_open is not None:
                break
        day += timedelta(days=1)
    return state, last_close, next_open


def refresh_after_for(symbols, now=None):
    """Seconds widget_command.sh waits before the next refresh, from the
    held and watched symbols' markets: REFRESH_OPEN while any is open,
    REFRESH_EDGE while any is in US pre/after hours and none is open,
    REFRESH_CLOSED otherwise (or with no symbols) — but never past the
    earliest next open (REFRESH_OPEN at least), so the first refresh of a
    session is not late."""
    now = int(now if now is not None else now_epoch())
    states, opens = set(), []
    for sym in dict.fromkeys(symbols or ()):
        try:
            state, _, nxt = symbol_session(sym, now)
        except Exception:
            continue
        states.add(state)
        if nxt is not None:
            opens.append(nxt)
    if "open" in states:
        secs = REFRESH_OPEN
    elif "pre" in states or "after" in states:
        secs = REFRESH_EDGE
    else:
        secs = REFRESH_CLOSED
    if opens:
        secs = min(secs, max(REFRESH_OPEN, min(opens) - now))
    return int(secs)


def split_currency(cur):
    """Quote currency -> (ISO code, multiplier into that code)."""
    if cur in MINOR_UNITS:
        return MINOR_UNITS[cur]
    return (str(cur or "USD").upper(), 1.0)


class FX:
    """Rates from each quote currency into the display currency. Yahoo's
    pair "EURUSD=X" is the price of 1 EUR in USD."""

    def __init__(self, display):
        self.display = display
        self.now = {display: 1.0}
        self.prev = {display: 1.0}
        self._series = {}   # (iso, "daily"|"intraday"|"hourly") -> (keys, rates)

    def symbol(self, iso):
        return "%s%s=X" % (iso, self.display)

    def add(self, iso, result):
        self.now[iso] = result["price"]
        self.prev[iso] = result.get("prevClose") or result["price"]
        for kind in ("daily", "intraday", "hourly"):
            pts = sorted(result.get(kind) or [])
            self._series[(iso, kind)] = ([k for k, _ in pts], [v for _, v in pts])

    def factor(self, cur, prev=False):
        """Multiplier from a price quoted in `cur` to the display currency,
        or None when no rate is known."""
        iso, mult = split_currency(cur)
        rate = (self.prev if prev else self.now).get(iso)
        return None if rate is None else rate * mult

    def factor_at(self, cur, key, kind):
        """Same, at a past moment: the last `kind` bar at or before `key`
        (a YYYY-MM-DD date for daily bars, an epoch otherwise)."""
        iso, mult = split_currency(cur)
        if iso == self.display:
            return mult
        keys, rates = self._series.get((iso, kind), ([], []))
        i = bisect.bisect_right(keys, key)
        if i:
            return rates[i - 1] * mult
        if rates:
            return rates[0] * mult
        rate = self.now.get(iso)
        return None if rate is None else rate * mult

    def daily_first(self, cur):
        """Date of the first daily rate bar for `cur`: "0000-00-00" for the
        display currency (always 1), None when there is no daily series."""
        iso = split_currency(cur)[0]
        if iso == self.display:
            return "0000-00-00"
        keys = self._series.get((iso, "daily"), ([], []))[0]
        return keys[0] if keys else None


def date_to_close_epoch(date_str):
    """Epoch for 16:00 ET on a YYYY-MM-DD date (used for daily-close points)."""
    d = datetime.strptime(date_str, "%Y-%m-%d")
    d = d.replace(hour=16, tzinfo=MARKET_TZ)
    return int(d.timestamp())

def ui_amount(value):
    """A finite amount > 0 (a number or numeric text, not true/false)
    rounded to 2 decimals (an int when whole), else None."""
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return None
    try:
        v = float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if not math.isfinite(v) or v <= 0:
        return None
    v = round(v, 2)
    return int(v) if v == int(v) else v


def ui_cash(value):
    """_cash as data.json's "ui" shows it: {ISO code upper-cased: amount}
    for 3-letter codes with an amount > 0; {} for anything else."""
    out = {}
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        return out
    for cur, amount in value.items():
        iso = str(cur).strip().upper()
        n = ui_amount(amount)
        if re.match(r"^[A-Z]{3}$", iso) and n is not None:
            out[iso] = n

    name listed twice), or None when unset, empty or unreadable."""

        return None
    try:
        import rebalance
        entries, _ = rebalance.parse_targets(value)
        out = {}
        for k, p in entries or []:

                out[k] = int(p) if p == int(p) else round(p, 2)

    except Exception:
        return None

def demo_kind(raw, example_path):
    """What the welcome card should say (13.5): "example" while the holdings
    are exactly the demo portfolio's (the same tickers as
    positions.example.json), "empty" while there are none at all, else None.
    Anything sold or a money-in figure means it is the owner's own: None, and
    so does a buy added to a demo stock (more lots than the example has)."""
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        return None
    if raw.get("_realized") or raw.get("_invested") is not None:
        return None
    held = {k.upper() for k in raw if isinstance(k, str) and not k.startswith("_")}
    if not held:
        return "empty"
    example = read_json(example_path, None)
    if not isinstance(example, dict):
        return None
    ex = {k.upper(): v for k, v in example.items() if isinstance(k, str) and not k.startswith("_")}
    if held != set(ex):
        return None

    def n_lots(entry):
        lots = entry.get("lots") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
        return len(lots) if isinstance(lots, list) else 1
    for k, v in raw.items():
        if isinstance(k, str) and not k.startswith("_") and n_lots(v) > n_lots(ex.get(k.upper())):
            return None
    return "example"


def is_demo(raw, example_path):
    """True while the welcome card shows: the demo portfolio's holdings or
    none at all (see demo_kind)."""
    return demo_kind(raw, example_path) is not None


def parse_version(text):
    """"v13.4" / "13.4.1" -> "13.4" / "13.4.1"; None for anything else."""
    m = re.match(r"^\s*v?(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\s*$", str(text or ""))
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def parse_release(obj):
    """A GitHub "latest release" object -> {latest, url, zip, published} or
    None when it has no usable tag."""
    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
        return None
    latest = parse_version(obj.get("tag_name") or obj.get("name"))
    if not latest:
        return None
    zip_url = None
    for a in obj.get("assets") or []:
        if isinstance(a, dict) and str(a.get("name") or "").endswith(".zip") \
                and str(a.get("browser_download_url") or "").startswith(("https://", "file://")):
            zip_url = a["browser_download_url"]
            break
    url = obj.get("html_url") if str(obj.get("html_url") or "").startswith("https://") else None
    pub = obj.get("published_at") if isinstance(obj.get("published_at"), str) else None
    return {"latest": latest, "url": url, "zip": zip_url, "published": pub}


def fetch_release():
    """The newest release's JSON from UPDATE_URL (PORTFOLIO_UPDATE_URL in
    tests). Raises on network trouble or bad JSON."""
    import urllib.request
    url = os.environ.get("PORTFOLIO_UPDATE_URL") or UPDATE_URL
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": NEWS_FEED_UA,
                                               "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json, application/json"})
    kw = {"context": feed_ssl_context()} if url.startswith("https://") else {}
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=UPDATE_TIMEOUT, **kw) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read(200000).decode("utf-8", "replace"))


def update_due(state, now, force=False):
    """Is a GitHub check due for update.json's `state`: never checked,
    UPDATE_TTL after a check that worked, UPDATE_RETRY after one that failed,
    or `force`. A check still "trying" (started less than UPDATE_RETRY ago,
    or cut off by the refresh's exit: it counts as a failed one) is not."""
    if force:
        return True
    if not isinstance(state, dict) or not state:
        return True
    trying = state.get("trying")
    if isinstance(trying, (int, float)) and not isinstance(trying, bool) \
            and 0 <= now - trying < UPDATE_RETRY:
        return False
    checked = state.get("checked") if isinstance(state.get("checked"), (int, float)) else 0
    return now - checked >= (UPDATE_TTL if state.get("ok") else UPDATE_RETRY)


def update_answer(state):
    """update.json's state -> {latest, url, zip, checked, ok}, or None when
    nothing is known yet (no state, or only a first check still trying)."""
    if not isinstance(state, dict):
        return None
    state = {k: v for k, v in state.items() if k != "trying"}
    if not parse_version(state.get("latest")):
        return {"latest": None, "url": None, "zip": None, "checked": state.get("checked"),
                "ok": state.get("ok") is True} if state else None
    return {"latest": state["latest"], "url": state.get("url"), "zip": state.get("zip"),
            "checked": state.get("checked"), "ok": state.get("ok") is True}


def read_update_cache(cache_dir, enabled=True):
    """The last known answer from .cache/update.json without asking GitHub
    (a refresh whose check is still running uses it); None when off."""
    if not enabled:
        return None
    return update_answer(read_json(os.path.join(cache_dir, "update.json"), None))


def check_update(cache_dir, enabled=True, now=None, force=False):
    """The cached answer of the update check, refreshed when due
    (update_due). Off (`enabled` False): None, and no request. Never raises;
    the cache keeps the last known release when a check fails. A due check
    first stamps "trying" into update.json, so one cut off by the refresh's
    exit waits UPDATE_RETRY instead of starting again on every refresh.
    -> {latest, url, zip, checked, ok} or None (nothing known yet)."""
    if not enabled and not force:
        return None
    now = int(now if now is not None else time.time())
    path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "update.json")
    state = read_json(path, None)
    if not isinstance(state, dict):
        state = {}
    if update_due(state, now, force):
        try:
            os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
            write_json(path, dict(state, trying=now))
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            rel = parse_release(fetch_release())
            if rel is None:
                raise ValueError("no release tag in the answer")
            state = {"checked": now, "ok": True, "latest": rel["latest"], "url": rel["url"],
                     "zip": rel["zip"], "published": rel["published"]}
        except Exception as e:
            state = {"checked": now, "ok": False, "error": str(e)[:200],
                     "latest": state.get("latest"), "url": state.get("url"), "zip": state.get("zip"),
                     "published": state.get("published")}
        try:
            os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
            write_json(path, state)       # a finished check: no "trying"
        except Exception:
            pass
    return update_answer(state)
